title: Approve the release in the browser and read the evidence that carried it
description:
SPIDR child 3 of task-2a345b2e97d94599b4688af1923056e5 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). dependsOn child 1 (task-70a7ccd3293f465fbc9c1888ae540f5d, the dossier this card summarises) and child 2 (task-f961dc899a13488da8f119abdc37631f, the kind and receipt it dispatches and renders). PROOF ROW for Gate 3: it owns the browser journey, the live PR, the docs sweep and the adversarial pass, so neither sibling files its own evidence row (global rail 21).

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the operator's side of Gate 3. A Release card on the opened goal showing the evidence summary (criteria covered n/m, receipts, landings, the preview decision), an Approve-release arm/confirm modelled on the PUBLISH card, and the PR link afterwards. Runs shows the release receipt. Needs-you lists goals ready for release.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb - every pattern exists, so this row composes:
- The arm/confirm card to model: apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/goal-publish.tsx (141 lines) with testids cr.publish.root/landed/state/link/unoffered, and publish-port.ts (22 lines) spending the offer.
- The decision wire: apps/control-room/src/v2/approvals/offer-wire.ts `spendOffer`, with escalation-port.ts (43 lines) as the tightest worked example.
- Needs-you: needs-you-model.ts:28 `NEEDS_YOU_KINDS` (a four-member roster) with the card in needs-you.tsx.
- The board/Runs feed: activity-words.ts maps a kind to operator words.

WORDS ARE THE PRODUCT. Gate 3 asks the human 'Is the evidence strong enough to expose this to users?' - the card asks THAT, and the evidence summary exists so the answer can be informed. An n/m that reads 'complete' while criteria rendered UNKNOWN in the dossier would be the worst defect this row could ship: the operator would approve a release believing evidence that was never measured. Surface the UNKNOWN count beside the covered count.
definitionOfDone: The Release card renders on a goal whose evidence is ready: criteria covered n/m WITH the UNKNOWN count shown separately when any criterion could not be re-measured, the verifier receipts and landing shas, and the preview decision or its explicit absence. A test asserts the UNKNOWN count is visible when the dossier carries one - a summary that folds UNKNOWN into 'covered' would let an operator approve unmeasured evidence.

Approve dispatches `release.decide` through the offer-wire `spendOffer` path (no second decision wire), with an arm/confirm modelled on the PUBLISH card; the PR link renders after a RELEASED receipt, and a REFUSED receipt renders its code VERBATIM - assert the literal RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE text and that the missing criterion ids reach the operator.

The card is ABSENT when the daemon offers no `release.decide`, rather than rendering a dead button - a control that dispatches into a refusal is worse than an honest explanation. Assert both the offered and un-offered states.
Needs-you lists a goal ready for release and stops listing it once released; Runs shows the release receipt. Assert appearance AND disappearance - a queue entry that never clears grows forever.

A Playwright journey against a REAL daemon covers evidence -> card -> approve -> PR link, with the `pnpm test:e2e:browser` count line quoted. Control-room fixtures are the daemon's REAL frames captured from that run (the exact-key decoders reject hand-written ones).

LIVE DRIVE: a real pull request opened on the UnAI remote or a throwaway GitHub repository, with the PR URL, the release receipt id and the dossier sha256 in a row comment under ~4500 chars. If `gh` is absent or unauthenticated on the lane, record the RELEASE_PR_FAILED refusal with its stderr line verbatim - that is a legitimate recorded outcome, never worked around and never a fabricated PR.

README's 'no release gate' clause and the VISION Stage 1 'proof-carrying PR' status line are rewritten to the measured truth; the runbook documents the `gh` prerequisite and its refusal. Gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:e2e:browser`.
taskRails: THIS ROW PROVES, IT DOES NOT REBUILD. If the card cannot render because the dossier or receipt is missing a member, comment on THAT child and report_blocked on it - do not add a daemon field here (global rail 4: a proof that repairs its own subject retires the question unanswered).
NEVER FOLD UNKNOWN INTO COVERED. The dossier deliberately renders unmeasurable evidence as UNKNOWN rather than dropping it; a summary that hides that distinction defeats child 1's whole design.
REUSE THE EXISTING PATTERNS: offer-wire `spendOffer` for the decision, the PUBLISH card's arm/confirm shape, the existing Needs-you roster. A second decision wire is a design regression.
REAL FRAMES ONLY: control-room fixtures come from a real daemon run; exact-key decoders reject hand-written frames, and the failure looks like a test bug rather than a fixture bug.

Check any new testid namespace is free before using it, keep JSX text ASCII-only and apostrophe-free (the scheduler package-boundary scan reds otherwise), and keep every production file under 250 lines.

Confirming rather than re-litigating, because 3 producer rows have moved since and the gap could plausibly have closed.

GAP, SYMBOL BY SYMBOL — commands and verbatim results:

1. `grep -rn "release\.decide" apps/ packages/ adapters/ --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx | wc -l` => `0`
2. `grep -rn "RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE\|RELEASE_PR_FAILED" apps/ packages/ adapters/ --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx | wc -l` => `0`
3. `find apps packages adapters -iname "*release*decide*"` => no output (no module owns the kind)

DoD clauses 2, 3 and 6 name those three symbols directly: clause 2 demands the literal `RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE` text be asserted and the missing criterion ids reach the operator; clause 3 demands the card be ABSENT when the daemon offers no `release.decide`, asserted in BOTH the offered and un-offered states; clause 6 demands `RELEASE_PR_FAILED` with its stderr line verbatim when `gh` is missing. None of those three literals exists on disk. A plan written now would have to invent the refusal codes, the offer shape and the receipt shape in the control-room, i.e. a mock-backed journey — forbidden by task rail 1 ("THIS ROW PROVES, IT DOES NOT REBUILD"), task rail 4 (REAL FRAMES ONLY: the exact-key decoders reject hand-written frames), and global rail 4 clause 2 ("a proof that only proves shapes retires the question unanswered; a falsely retired gate cannot be repaired").

WHAT IS ACTUALLY READY — this row is NOT blocked on its own composition surface, only on the kind:
- Child 1 IS landed: `apps/daemon/src/release/` holds release-dossier{,-contracts,-ledger,-sections}.ts each with its .js bridge, plus 2 test files. task-70a7ccd3 DONE at 1c464208, reviewSummary confirms 30/30.

Note the path: the description says needs-you-model.ts:28 without the `approvals/` segment; it lives under v2/approvals/, not v2/needs-you/. Adding a member here is a roster change, so global rail 19 applies — needs-you-model.test.ts and needs-you.test.tsx must be in affectedFiles, and any hard-coded length assertion re-counted.
- Testid namespace `cr.release.*` is FREE: `grep -rn "cr\.release" apps/control-room/src tests | wc -l` => `0`. Safe to claim (task rail 5).

So the leaf-first order holds and only the kind is missing. Blocking on the 3 rows that own it rather than filing anything new (global rail 20: a row already owns the capability).
